text:
maya: FYI customer 'acme' is seeing intermittent 429/503s on their Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-3) starting ~08:40 UTC. They report 'throttled' errors and high tail latency. I grabbed a short log excerpt below.

maya: ```
2026-03-15T08:42:11Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 tenant=acme model=redwood-7b path=/v1/generate status=429 reason=kv_cache_pressure evicts=1187 kv_mem_bytes=1148234567
2026-03-15T08:42:12Z WARN  evict_strategy=async_lru compaction=false fragmentation=0.72
```

sam: thanks. Do we know workload shape? long contexts or big system prompts?

maya: customer is doing multi-session long-context chat — pinned history + streaming. They run ~20 concurrent streams, many with 80k-120k token contexts.

caroline: soundslike KV saturation. Any recent config changes on that pool? autoscaler/policy?

maya: autoscaler is standard dedicated policy (scale_delay=120s, burst_enabled=true). No recent deploys according to deploy-bot.

ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-nyc-3: node-7 mem_used=94% gpu_mem=88% kv_evictions=1320 rate=throttled

ingrid: fragmentation ~0.7 in the logs — we've seen long-lived large KV entries cause fragmentation and slow GC which delays reclaiming bytes. That prevents new insertions and triggers throttling.

sam: repro plan — can one of you run a local repro: 30 concurrent streams with repeated system+history to hit KV churn. I can also try on staging with a tenant-scoped env var to force long-prefix behavior.

maya: repro steps I used: 
1) create tenant header X-Tenant: acme-repro
2) POST /v1/generate with payload that prefixes a 60k token system prompt, then stream 30 concurrent requests for 10 minutes.

curl example: ```bash
for i in {1..30}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate" 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" 
    -H "X-Tenant: acme-repro" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"'"$(python -c 'print("system:\\n"+"A"*60000)')"'","max_new_tokens":32}' &
done
```

caroline: Thanks — customer is asking for a hotfix. Short-term options: 1) temporary per-tenant kv quota + reject large-context requests, 2) increase pool capacity (provision 1-2 nodes), 3) roll an LRU/compaction patch to force more aggressive reclamation.

sam: Agree. Immediate stopgap: raise tenant quota for acme by 2x for 2 hours and ask them to reduce max_context. I'll open a capacity bump ticket.

ingrid: For the patch route: there's a lightweight change to trigger synchronous compaction on high-frag nodes (kv-compact-quick) — low risk, can canary to a single node in the pool. Monitor evicts and fragmentation.

maya: I'll tell customer we are provisioning capacity and asking for reduced context as we test the kv-compact canary.

caroline: I've submitted support action: ticket #SUP-2987, temporary quota bump requested. Oncall: @sam — can you schedule canary and add metrics watch: kv_evictions, kv_fragmentation, request_429_rate?

sam: Scheduling canary now — will route 5% of acme traffic to node-7 with kv-compact-quick enabled, start at 08:55 UTC and monitor for 20m.

ops-bot: [action] canary_deploy started canary_id=canary-482 node=node-7 config=kv-compact-quick

maya: thanks. I'll update the customer with repro steps and timeline. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem if needed. :thumbsup:
